title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: The rule of one country over another people and land, to control and use them.

en.text: After the slave trade ended, the "legitimate trade" and European industry led to the New Imperialism and the Scramble for Africa; the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 set rules for claiming land. Africans resisted everywhere — Samori Toure, the Ashanti, Urabi Pasha, the Mahdists, Maji-Maji — but only Ethiopia won, at Adwa in 1896. Britain ruled through indirect rule (Lugard) and France through assimilation and direct rule (Sarraut), and colonial economies turned Africa into a source of cash crops and minerals.

am.text: የባሪያ ንግድ ካበቃ በኋላ አውሮፓ አፍሪካን ተቀራመተች። አፍሪካውያን ተቃወሙ፤ ኢትዮጵያ ብቻ በዓድዋ አሸነፈች። እንግሊዝ ቀጥተኛ ያልሆነ፣ ፈረንሳይ ቀጥተኛ አገዛዝ ተጠቀሙ።

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Ending the slave trade took about half a century; Britain led it.
Industrial Britain wanted Africans to stay in Africa, produce raw materials and buy European goods.
The scramble began slowly in the 1870s and peaked in the late 1880s and 1890s.
The Berlin Conference (1884–85) made powers notify each other of claims.
Africans resisted: Samori Toure, Urabi Pasha, the Mahdists, Maji-Maji.
Britain used indirect rule (Lugard); France used direct rule (Sarraut).

screens.title: Mau Mau in Kenya
paras: Review question 4 asks about Mau Mau; the unit does not teach it.
Mau Mau (1952–1960) was an armed struggle against British rule in Kenya.
It was led mainly by the Kikuyu of central Kenya.
They fought white settlers' seizure of their land.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The rule of one country over another people and land, to control and use them.

screens.title: Put these events in order
screens.why: Partition first, then resistance, then the age of colonial administration.
screens.clue: Adwa and Omdurman are two years apart.

screens.title: Match each person with what they are known for
screens.clue: Two are administrators, two are European rulers, two are African rulers.

screens.text: Which statement about the Berlin Conference is TRUE?
opts: It set rules for claiming land; the rush to occupy came after it
It drew every African border in one meeting
screens.ans: It set rules for claiming land; the rush to occupy came after it
screens.why: p.31, p.33: notification and effective occupation; the competitive rush followed.

screens.text: Review Q5 asks what has been a serious political problem for independent African states. Which answer is best supported by this unit?
opts: Colonial boundaries drawn by Europeans without Africans, and "tribal" divisions
The end of the slave trade
screens.ans: Colonial boundaries drawn by Europeans without Africans, and "tribal" divisions
screens.why: No African state was at Berlin, so borders split or joined peoples; "divide and rule" stressed "tribal" rivalries.

items.ask: The British colonial policy was designed by ___
items.why: p.40: indirect rule was "most clearly formulated by Frederick Luggard" (Lugard).

items.ask: Direct rule was the colonial policy of the ___
items.why: p.45: "The French pursued a colonial administrative policy known as Direct Rule." (Germany also used it.)

items.ask: The anti-colonial struggle in West Africa against the French was led by ___
The Mau Mau was an anti-colonial movement in ___
items.why: Mau Mau (1952–1960) fought British rule and settler land seizure in Kenya (see the added summary box).
items.clue: An East African country ruled by Britain, home of the Kikuyu.

items.ask: ___ have been a serious political problem for independent African states
items.why: Borders drawn by Europeans without Africans split or joined peoples; "divide and rule" stressed "tribal" rivalries.
items.clue: Think of the lines drawn at and after Berlin.

test.text: The European power that colonized Tanganyika before 1914 was
Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa in

opts: the Urabi revolt and riots in Alexandria
test.ans: the Urabi revolt and riots in Alexandria

test.text: Why did the "effective occupation" rule lead to more wars of conquest?
opts: Powers had to occupy land physically to keep their claims
It gave land only to Ethiopia
test.ans: Powers had to occupy land physically to keep their claims

notes.text: Review Q4 (Mau Mau, Kenya) is not covered anywhere in Unit 2; a short added box explains Mau Mau so students can answer it.
Review Q5 is open-ended; the unit never states the expected word. The blank accepts colonial boundaries/border problems and tribalism/ethnic divisions.
p.44 summary: "if the British remain in Africa" should read "if the black people remained in Africa" (to produce raw materials and buy European goods); the lesson uses the corrected sense.
